title: Minimax Regret for Deterministic Dose Choice When the Optimizer Approaches Vanishing Overlap
banked_reason: The one-dimensional, globally strongly concave model and absence of an application limit the package’s significance for a leading econometrics journal.
gap_reasons: The one-dimensional, globally strongly concave model and absence of an application limit the package’s significance for a leading econometrics journal.

The causal result is conditional on the all-dose bridge equating potential-outcome means with the observed regression, so it adds a welfare interpretation rather than a separate identification result.

The reproduced observed-to-causal transfer uses only the all-dose bridge and bounded observed response; neither upper nor lower route needs bounded counterfactual outcomes, so this clause materially narrows the causal frontier without a consumed proof step.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the observed-law minimax expected-regret frontier min{(tbar-delta_n)^2, h_n^(2 beta-2)} with n h_n^(2 beta+1)(delta_n+h_n)^kappa=1, using a split-sample local-polynomial rule and a bounded Bernoulli testing pair, then transferred it exactly to causal welfare under the all-dose bridge. The result remained sound but below the field floor because the final package was one-dimensional, globally strongly concave, and lacked a developed application; removing the unused bounded-counterfactual assumption is faithful cleanup but does not change the tier. A field-level continuation requires genuinely new individualized or multistratum, local-curvature or unknown-smoothness theory and an application, rather than another repair of this anchor.
tldr: The observed-law minimax regression-regret frontier is \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\asymp\min\{w^2,h^{2\beta-2}\}\), where \(nh^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h)^\kappa=1\). A count-selected, split-sample local-polynomial rule attains it under a merely measurable polynomial density envelope. The same rate holds for identified causal welfare regret because the all-dose bridge identifies the causal dose response, and bounded Bernoulli potential-outcome laws realize the testing lower bound.
gap: The closest verified passive optimization benchmark has a positive design floor for its upper theorem, while its separate lower theorem uses bounded density and additive-noise regularity. The published Ziegler 2004 random-design mode article and its precise restatement of the 2002/2003 antecedents use a fixed interior mode and a positive density floor. The inspected record does not give uniform expected optimizer regret when the optimum moves toward a polynomially thinned boundary; original 2002/2003 full texts remain inaccessible.
fill: Establish the matching order \(\min\{w^2,h^{2\beta-2}\}\), a legal Bernoulli testing submodel, and a feasible count-selected pilot-plus-polynomial rule uniformly across the moving overlap transition.
